> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR

> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **151** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7265b33e779e1d63afe50fb86e411beda7582838` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f34af0988cebc62ddf388bb9fe459e09d813ee79` — the merge of head `37a9e0fee342606e7c11b2c5877e27c009a22d28` into base `7265b33e779e1d63afe50fb86e411beda7582838`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f34af0988cebc62ddf388bb9fe459e09d813ee79 && git checkout f34af0988cebc62ddf388bb9fe459e09d813ee79
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7265b33e779e1d63afe50fb86e411beda7582838 37a9e0fee342606e7c11b2c5877e27c009a22d28 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7265b33e779e1d63afe50fb86e411beda7582838 && git merge --no-ff 37a9e0fee342606e7c11b2c5877e27c009a22d28

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7265b33e779e1d63afe50fb86e411beda7582838
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7265b33e779e1d63afe50fb86e411beda7582838` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The `docs/audits/…counts/system.md` 377 → 378 row is the strictness ledger the gate regenerates (spec lane), and `content/docs/references/system/translation.mdx` is generated. No governed path, no `content/docs/releases/`. Mergeable with no conflict.
2. **The card's asks, measured on the diff.** (a) Address: `_sections.SECTION.fields.FIELD.{label,placeholder,helpText}`, strict, one convention with `_sections`. The aliases (`entries` → `fields`; `help` / `hint` / `tooltip` → `helpText`) are refusal-with-rename prescriptions, not new accepted spellings. (b) `translateFormSectionEntries` follows the section rules: authored copy only (`sectionCopyAuthored`), a missing key keeps the authored string, and an override on the packaged view keeps the edit (`valueOverridesPackagedBase`, ADR-0029 D9.2a). A section with no `name` and a bare field-name entry have no key. (c) The extractor scaffolds the key, and coverage reads the same walker. (d) `translation-target-unknown` reports an entry key that no form-view section of that name declares, and points a bare-field entry at `objects.OBJECT.fields.FIELD`. The door pins (zh-CN serves translated entry copy; a missing key and en serve authored copy) and one `translateView` pin per key are in the tests.
3. **Gates.** Check-runs on `37a9e0fee3` at this record: 26 success, 6 skipped, 8 in progress, 0 failed. Local, per the report: `--ran` 117 derived, 116 run, 1 NOT MEASURED (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, declared; CI runs it). Spec full suite in three chunks, lint 158 files, cli unit narrowed to 33 extractor-reaching files (declared), rest 5 suites / 128 tests. Ablation on the entry walker: 5/23 red, then restored. Landing waits for every check green and the contract-review PASS.
4. **Deviations accepted.** (a) The branch was opened on base `8801f2bb37` with no `origin/main` merge before the PR, and it is 10 commits behind with no conflict. The merge queue tests the merged result; this is not repeated as a rework. (b) The cli unit tier and the spec suite were narrowed or chunked for the foreground cap, declared. (c) The first push was refused for a model-named trailer and amended to the model-free pair before publishing. (d) The PR body footer follows the harness's attribution form rather than the role file's session-URL footer: a cosmetic gap, not re-worked. `mcp_calls` 0; relay writes 2. Container overhead for the card log: install 39 s + build closure 588 s = 627 s wall, with no turbo remote-cache pull.
5. **Out-of-scope outcomes.**
   - An inline locale map on an entry string takes the catalog when the pack has a key (the section precedent); the console rendering of such a map is not measured: Acceptance notes (already in the PR body).
   - A nameless, heading-less section whose entries author copy has no address and no warning: Acceptance notes (extending `validate-translatable-sections` is a new warning face, outside the card).
   - Sub-fields of a composite or repeater entry have no address: Acceptance notes (no producer measured).
   - `check:query-options-erasure` (> 400 s locally) and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (whole-workspace build) are CI-shaped gates the derivation lists for a spec diff: dropped — an observation about local cost, with no wrong answer.
   - The cross-lane note for the `packages/cli` and `packages/rest` riders is posted on seat post #6021 (`6383123807`).
6. **Landing.** Not governed and under 3000 changed lines. Once the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS is on record and every check on the then-current head is green, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay. On merge, objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2248 can be reopened against the release that carries it.
